qc.label_under_test: ' late' in the phrase 'too late' (a missed chance); plain temporal 'late', 'too early/soon' and 'never too late' stay near background. Separate second trigger: therapy/psychology vocabulary (not covered by this test)

neighbours.label: Dense / gate-leak background unit: the - pole is a weak leak (max 1.52, 11% of tokens above 0.1 of max, 99.6% '-g +u leak') that hums at about 0.1-0.3 of max on most prose. Its feeders ('late' in any sense, lateness words, 'belated', 'little', ambient-it predicates) add only a small bump, so 'too late' / 'too little, too late' does not separate from matched text without lateness; the slightly stronger pockets are clinical-psychology / talking-therapy text (the + pole's topic leaking through) and the headline 'Too Little too Late?'.
fire: The rescue team reached the valley too late to stop the flood.
Too little, too late: the fans booed the club's last-minute signing.
She realised too late that the ticket was for the wrong day.
The vaccine order came too late for the first wave.
Critics called the climate pledge too little, too late.
By the time he called back, it was too late to fix the mistake.
The warning was issued too late for most residents to leave.
Is it too late to apologise to her now?
quiet: The rescue team reached the valley early and stopped the flood.
The fans cheered the club's new signing at the stadium.
She realised quickly that the ticket was for the wrong day.
The vaccine order arrived in time for the first wave.
Critics called the climate pledge bold and well funded.
When he called back, they fixed the mistake together.
The warning was issued in time for most residents to leave.
Is it a good time to call her now?
